title: fastpath: add gating + precision-toggle with safe-mode fallback for KV cache and continuous batching
author: Jordan Patel
description:
Motivation: fastpath execution gives large perf wins but exposes correctness risk for some model constructs (torch/transformer fused kernels, FP16 quantization edge cases, KV cache invalidation under interleaved requests). This PR adds a gating mechanism that prefers the fastpath when a set of runtime checks pass, a runtime precision-toggle to select safer numerics for problematic sequences, and an explicit 'safe-mode' fallback that forces the conservative path when heuristics or CI detect anomalies. Summary of changes: - fastpath gating: runtime guards based on model metadata, sequence length, KV cache age, and op-level compatibility table. - precision toggle: per-request header to prefer FP16/AMP fast kernels or fall back to FP32-safe kernels; persisted as an execution hint to routing. - safe-mode: system-level toggle (cluster and request-scoped) that disables fastpath and forces conservative kernels/batching behavior for correctness-first windows. - KV cache: fixes around cache invalidation ordering for continuous batching when requests race across worker shards; introduces a lightweight stamp to ensure monotonic cache updates. - batching/scheduler: updated scheduler to include gating decisions in batch formation, avoiding mixing safe and fast requests; small scheduler refactor to reduce tail latency when safe-mode is active. Why this approach: we saw transient correctness regressions in staging when mixing quantized fastpath and long-history KV lookups; purely disabling fastpath regressed latency ~10-20%. The gating + toggle approach aims to preserve most perf wins while providing operational levers for correctness. Checklist:
- [x] fastpath gating unit tests
- [x] precision toggle end-to-end tests (model runner)
- [x] KV cache race condition tests
- [x] integration test in perf-canary harness
- [x] docs + release notes entry
Notes: The description includes a short ops playbook in README runtime docs about enabling safe-mode per-queue and recommended heuristics for canarying fastpath. Linear: ENG-3921 tracks rollout plan and dashboarding.

review_comments: Mei Chen: Overall looks good. Two requests: 1) can we add a metric for number of safe-mode fallbacks per-minute (to monitor rollback triggers) 2) add a small benchmark across three representative models showing delta when gating is enabled vs disabled.
Author (Jordan Patel): Added metrics and added perf-canary job that runs three models; results uploaded to the PR artifacts. See commit t6u7v8w.
Diego Alvarez: Found a race in the initial KV stamp implementation that could cause double-invalidate; thanks for the fix in h7i8j9k. Verified with deterministic replay logs.
Priya Natarajan: Approved after verifying scheduler doesn't mix safe/fast requests in a batch. Left a minor nit about log verbosity in gating.rs that we can address in follow-up.
CI: initial run had a flaky transformer test failing on macOS runners; rerun succeeded. All required checks passed.
release_notes: Introduce fastpath gating and precision toggle with safe-mode fallback. Improves tail latency by allowing fast kernels when safe while providing an ops-level switch to force correctness-first execution. Includes KV cache race fixes and scheduler batching separation to avoid mixing safe and fast requests.
